name: Bosngun
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: SIL-PNG language resources page for bqs (2015 snapshot) and OLAC listing for bqs (2024 snapshot).
sources.note: Catalog pages: SIL-PNG had 'Nothing yet available' for Bosmun; OLAC lists only Capell estate recordings, Rosetta/TransNewGuinea wordlists, Paris 2015 and Foley's WF3-010 audio -- no grammar, phonology or OPD exists in these catalogs.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). transnewguinea.org: Bosmun (62 items, all from Foley 2005).
sources.note: Lexical forms without stress marks; data only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Bosman = sect. 2.23.11.15, p.75; Ottilien typological characteristics 2.23.11.3, p.76)
sources.note: Explicitly omits stress for all languages surveyed: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' (intro to the typological notes). Ottilien/Bosman typological notes list segmental features only (glottal stop word-finally, /n/ [ɲ?] phoneme in Bosman, high central vowel, no /f/).

sources.citation: Paris, Brian. 2015. A sociolinguistic survey of the Lower Ramu languages of Papua New Guinea (Awar [aya], Bosmun [bqs], Kayan [kct], and Marangis [wax]). SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-009. Dallas: SIL International. 45 pp.
sources.note: Vitality/sociolinguistic survey only; no phonology, no wordlist. Its 'previous research' section for Bosmun names only von Poser's ethnographic work.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 572.
sources.note: Comparative WAG/Ottilien cognate tables with Bosmun forms; discusses Bosmun palatalisation, truncation, seven-vowel system; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1952. Languages of Bogia District, New Guinea [part 2]. Oceania 22(3): 178-207 (comparative vocabularies, Bosngun column pp. 198ff).
sources.note: No statement; the Bosngun wordlist is stress-marked item by item (e.g. 'panan head, 'lamak eye, 'nimbit blood, sa'yak fire, we'lay coconut, pe'lay dog, 'ngwa:rak bird) -- mixed initial and non-initial marks, data only.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1952. Languages of Bogia District: corrigenda. Oceania 22(4): 317.
sources.note: Corrigenda to Anaberg/Atemble forms only; nothing on Bosngun.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1951. Languages of Bogia District, New Guinea [part 1]. Oceania 22(2): 130-147 (Bosngun-Nubia sketch pp. 135-138).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Nothing for Bosngun-Nubia: the 'phonic structure' paragraph (pp.135-136) gives a consonant/vowel chart, notes on glottal stop, labiodental v, cerebral r and a rare mixed vowel, but no stress remark. General intro (pp.130-131) says of all the Bogia languages 'None of them is tonal'. Capell does give stress notes for other languages in the same article (Watam p.132 'tendency to final stress'; Murusapa p.144 'Stress tends to be antepenultimate'), so the silence for Bosngun is real, not an scanned gap. Example sentences carry stress marks (e.g. we'lay'woro va'nay, tian'tay).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Most recent survey of Lower Sepik-Ramu by the only linguist with first-hand Bosmun data (his WF3-010 recordings); its Lower Ramu/Ottilien typological section is the likeliest place for any published remark on Bosmun or Ottilien word stress.
